# `nlink-lab events`

A drift line (`events -f --source drift`) names what changed in a node,
`<action>_<object>`, and its fields. A rule added or deleted by hand comes
with its text, as `nft -s list` prints it (`nft` in the JSON record), when
nlink can print it:

```text
2026-10-23T09:12:03Z drift fw:new_nft_rule chain=input family=inet handle=9 table=nlink-lab: tcp dport 22 accept
```

## Reference

<!-- cli-ref:start (generated by `nlink-lab docs-gen`; do not edit) -->

```text
Show a lab's lifecycle log (deploy, apply, spawn, kill, impair, partition, snapshot, …); `--follow` merges live drift (RTNETLINK / nftables) and runtime (process exit, link state) events, optionally fanned out on a unix socket.

JSON OUTPUT (with `--json`): one record per line tagged `source: lifecycle | drift | runtime`. Schema: docs/json-schemas/events.schema.json

Usage: nlink-lab events [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -L, --lab <LAB>
          The lab. Default: `$NLINK_LAB`, then the one `nlink-lab use` selected, then the only running lab

  -f, --follow
          Keep running: tail new lifecycle events and merge live drift (RTNETLINK and nftables changes in the nodes) and runtime events (process exits, interface state). Drift and runtime need root; without it only the lifecycle log is followed

      --source <SOURCE>
          Only these sources (repeatable; default all): `lifecycle` (what nlink-lab did), `drift` (kernel changes, live: with -f), `runtime` (process exits and link state, live: with -f). `-f --source drift` is what `watch` was
          
          [possible values: lifecycle, drift, runtime]

      --family <FAMILY>
          Drift: the netlink family to watch
          
          [default: both]
          [possible values: route, nftables, both]

      --node <NODE>
          Drift: one node only (nothing else is subscribed)

      --include-snapshot
          Drift: also show the resync replay after an ENOBUFS recovery (marked `[snapshot]`)

      --since <DURATION>
          Only events newer than this (`10m`, `2h`, `30s`)

      --kind <KIND>
          Only these event kinds (repeatable): lifecycle names such as `deployed`, `impaired`, `spawned`; drift names, `<action>_<object>` as drift records name them (`new_address`, `del_route`, `new_nft_rule`) or `ended`/`gone`; or the sources `lifecycle`, `drift`, `runtime`

  -i, --interval <DURATION>
          Runtime-event sampling interval (with --follow)
          
          [default: 2s]

      --socket <PATH>
          Also serve the stream on a unix socket: every client that connects receives one NDJSON record per line (with --follow)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

<!-- cli-ref:end -->
